value.body: A production chemist oversees chemical processes on a plant floor so each batch is made safely, on time and to specification. Chemical, pharmaceutical (API), agrochemical, dye and paint manufacturers hire them. A day involves running reactors and batches, recording parameters, coordinating with QC and following safety procedures.

items.label: Key documents
items.value: Batch manufacturing records, SOPs, material safety data sheets

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join as trainee or junior chemists at plants, mostly through walk-in drives, referrals and placement at colleges near industrial clusters. An M.Sc can lead to a higher starting grade.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Running batch processes and unit operations
Recording process data in batch records
Basic troubleshooting of yields and deviations
Coordinating with QC, maintenance and stores

value.title: At a glance
items: Jobs cluster in industrial belts and are plant-based.
Common next roles: shift in-charge, production officer, production manager.
Exposure to hazardous chemicals makes safety training central to the role.
